s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral nasal obstruction with purulent discharge and facial pain
salient_findings: Markedly hypertrophic left middle turbinate with granulomatous mucosa
Complete opacification of the ipsilateral maxillary, ethmoid, and frontal sinuses
key_facts: 55-year-old woman
History of diabetes mellitus
3-month history of left-sided nasal obstruction
Purulent nasal discharge
Facial pain
No improvement after multiple courses of oral antibiotics
No recent dental procedures or facial trauma
Anterior rhinoscopic examination showed purulent rhinorrhea
Hypertrophic left middle turbinate with granulomatous mucosa
Noncontrast computed tomography of the paranasal sinuses revealed a heterogeneous, focally hyperdense lesion

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral nasal obstruction with purulent discharge and facial pain
salient_findings: Markedly hypertrophic left middle turbinate with granulomatous mucosa
Complete opacification of the ipsilateral maxillary, ethmoid, and frontal sinuses

History of diabetes mellitus

Purulent nasal discharge
Facial pain
No improvement after multiple courses of oral antibiotics

shortlist.label: Chronic invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of diabetes mellitus and presentation of purulent nasal discharge, facial pain, and granulomatous mucosa are consistent with chronic invasive fungal sinusitis.

shortlist.label: Allergic fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of nasal obstruction, purulent discharge, and facial pain, along with the presence of a heterogeneous, focally hyperdense lesion on CT scan, are consistent with allergic fungal sinusitis.

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation of granulomatous mucosa, nasal obstruction, and purulent discharge could be indicative of granulomatosis with polyangiitis, although it is less likely given the absence of systemic symptoms.

shortlist.label: Acute invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Although the patient's 3-month history of symptoms suggests a chronic rather than acute process, acute invasive fungal sinusitis cannot be entirely ruled out, especially given the patient's history of diabetes mellitus and the presence of purulent rhinorrhea.

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of nasal obstruction and granulomatous mucosa could be consistent with sarcoidosis, although it is less likely given the absence of other systemic symptoms and the presence of a focal lesion on CT scan.

raw.rationale: The patient's history of diabetes mellitus, which is an immunocompromised state, combined with the presence of a heterogeneous, focally hyperdense lesion on CT scan and granulomatous mucosa on rhinoscopic examination, suggests an invasive fungal infection. The lack of improvement with antibiotics and the presence of purulent discharge also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: The 3-month duration of symptoms is relatively short for a chronic condition

rejected.label: Allergic fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging findings are more suggestive of an invasive process rather than an allergic reaction

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more localized to the sinuses and do not suggest a systemic vasculitis

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging findings are more suggestive of a fungal infection rather than a granulomatous disease like sarcoidosis
